In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of carbon metabolism in the green alga Selenastrun minutum.
the regulation of carbon flow in photosynthetic organisms, particularly in the green alga, Selenastrum.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
S. minutum PFK is an enzyme which is activated during carbon flux through the biosynthetic pathway and is inhibited during carbon flux through catabolic pathways.
Selenastrum PFK is a plastidic enzyme which is similar in many respects to the PFKs from higher plants and fungi.
the PFK of S. minutum is an allosteric enzyme that is subject to regulation in vivo by allosteric effectors, by phosphorylation, by aggregation state, and by the presence of other proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PFK is an allosteric enzyme that is subject to regulation by several metabolites and is probably the most important enzyme in the regulation of carbon flux through the Calvin cycle.
the algal plastidic PFRK is an unusual enzyme in that it has a high affinity for ATP and fructose-6-P and is subject to regulation by phosphate and other metabolites.
the PFK from S. minutum is a homotetrmeric enzyme that can aggregate to form a large complex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PFK is a major control point in the biosynthetic carbon flow in the green algal plastid.
PFK activity is regulated by the ratio of phosphoenol pyruvate and 3-phospho glycerate to phosphate.
the algal enzyme represents an evolutionary link between pyrophosphate dependent and ATP dependent PFKs.
